content: Metronidazole should not be administered to individuals who have a known history of hypersensitivity to metronidazole itself or to other nitroimidazole derivatives. Additionally, in patients diagnosed with trichomoniasis, the use of FLAGYL 375 capsules is strictly contraindicated during the first trimester of pregnancy. The concurrent use of oral metronidazole and disulfiram has been associated with the development of psychotic reactions in alcoholic patients. Therefore, metronidazole must not be given to patients who have taken disulfiram within the preceding two weeks. Oral metronidazole can cause a disulfiram-like reaction when alcohol is consumed. This reaction may manifest as abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing. Patients should avoid consuming alcohol or any products containing propylene glycol during treatment with metronidazole and for at least three days after completing the therapy.
